primary_sources: Modern Developer Portfolio UX Best Practices

rules.explanation: Providing dark/light theme options and clear sticky navigation enhances user experience across different screen conditions.
rules.do: Include a visible, working Dark/Light mode toggle and persistent header navigation for key sections.
rules.dont: Do not use fixed low-contrast colors that fail WCAG accessibility guidelines or hide main menu links.

rules.explanation: Recruiters often want to grab a copy of your CV immediately without opening multiple tabs.
rules.do: Provide a direct, high-visibility download button for your PDF resume in both the top navigation and contact sections.
rules.dont: Do not redirect users to external drive links requiring permissions or multi-step downloads.

rules.explanation: Allowing reviewers to filter showcased projects by specific technology (e.g., Python, C++, Machine Learning, Embedded) speeds up targeted evaluation.
rules.do: Implement category tag filters on the project grid for rapid sorting by skill/language.
rules.dont: Do not force reviewers to manually scroll through irrelevant projects to find specific tech stack examples.

rules.explanation: Integrating lightweight analytics allows candidates to track portfolio traffic, recruiter visits, and geographic interest.
rules.do: Add privacy-friendly analytics (e.g., Google Analytics or Vercel Analytics) to monitor profile reach.
rules.dont: Do not overload the page with heavy third-party tracking scripts that degrade page performance.
